correctness.rationale: The SPD spectral inequality lambda^2<=(kappa+1)lambda-kappa leads to x*Ax/(||Ax||||x||)>=2sqrt(kappa)/(kappa+1). A symmetric squared-norm embedding compresses E=S^TS-I to operator norm <=epsilon on the Krylov-next subspace, giving Re(y*Gy)>=(c-epsilon)||ABy||||By||>0, hence G invertible, F positive definite and Re eigenvalue(F,G)>0 for every m. For nonscalar A the endpoint eigenvector plane gives G=q(2q-epsilon(q^2+1)), F=q^2(q^2+1-2epsilon q)>0 (q=sqrt kappa); G vanishes at epsilon=c and is negative above. When kappa=1, c=1 and all permitted distortions are safe. Independent symbolic exact identities and 180 seeded 5x5 multi-step SPD Krylov samples confirmed the computations, but finite sampling is not treated as a universal proof.
